assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, followed by evidence for individual sources (the blazar TXS 0506+056 in 2017-2018 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068, plus the Galactic plane), opened neutrino astronomy as a new observational window and addressed the long-standing question of where cosmic rays are accelerated. The instrument, a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice, is a bold experimental achievement of the kind the physics prize has recognised before. From an instrumentation standpoint the originality lies in the concept and in the engineering of drilling, optical modules and ice calibration.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is widely regarded as the scientific driving force and principal investigator behind the concept and construction of IceCube, and Karle is credited with key detector, drilling and optical-sensor development. Yoshida is also credited, but I would not assume he is decisive; allocation among a 300-plus-member collaboration is the real difficulty, and a two-person prize would leave out many instrumental contributors, including the AMANDA predecessor team. I propose two of the three supplied names, acknowledging this is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by several analyses and independent channels, and the first source associations have held up for several years, though the TXS association rests on a modest chance-coincidence significance. KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD are only now providing independent confirmation. Recognition is timely: the field is established but still maturing.
uncertainties: Source associations beyond NGC 1068 and TXS 0506+056 are statistically limited and the interpretation of the diffuse flux (Galactic versus extragalactic, hadronic mechanisms) is not settled.
Credit allocation between the IceCube founders and the AMANDA pioneers is unresolved, and I rely on my own recollection of individual roles rather than verified records.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and demonstrated with Sr and later Yb, took frequency metrology to a fractional uncertainty of the order of 1e-18. It is a clear, original and lasting concept with direct consequences for fundamental physics, including tests of constancy of constants, searches for dark-matter signatures, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The clarity of the underlying idea is high.
assessment.attribution: The attribution is clean: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice approach, and Ye's group developed the clocks to the highest performance and demonstrated many of the most important physics applications. The supplied credit supports a natural two-person configuration. Hall and Hansch were recognised in 2005 for the frequency comb that these clocks rely on, so there is no overlap in the discovery itself.
assessment.maturity: The result has been independently confirmed by many groups worldwide and the uncertainty improvement is well documented. Timing is good, although the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: Some may judge that the ion-clock and single-ion line of work (already partly recognised in 2012 for ion control) leaves an ambiguous scope boundary.
Whether a clock technology is felt to be physics discovery or metrology invention is a matter for committee taste.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene showed that flat bands from moire superlattices produce correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable, carbon-only platform. It opened the entire field of twistronics and moire quantum matter, with a large body of follow-up work. The theoretical prediction of the magic angle followed by decisive experiments is a satisfying, clean story of prediction and confirmation.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the decisive experiments. This theory-experiment split gives a natural three-person configuration. Cao and Fatemi as first authors, and others who explored related twisted structures, may raise allocation questions that the supplied credit does not address.
assessment.maturity: Experiments have been reproduced across many groups, though sample-to-sample variation is large and the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated. The field is young for a prize but the prediction-confirmation pair is strong.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is unresolved, which may argue for waiting.
Credit to the earlier theoretical work on twisted-bilayer electronic structure, and to the students and postdocs who made the first devices, is not captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts settled the decades-old distance problem and established their cosmological origin and association with galaxies and later supernovae. This transformed gamma-ray burst science from a mystery into a branch of astrophysics and cosmology, and it is a textbook example of an instrument-driven discovery. I note my own professional familiarity with gamma-ray instrumentation, and I attempt to apply the same standard as for other candidates.
assessment.attribution: The BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and Narrow Field Instruments provided rapid localisations and the first X-ray afterglow (Costa, Frontera, and colleagues), and optical and radio follow-up established redshifts and a cosmological distance. Kulkarni led the radio and optical identification effort. Other key contributors, notably van Paradijs and the Caltech/Palomar and Mt Stromlo optical teams, as well as Metzger, Djorgovski and Frail, are not on this list, so the configuration is not clean and may be disputed.
assessment.maturity: The discovery dates from 1997 and has been confirmed thoroughly by Swift, Fermi and many other missions, so scientific maturity is high. The recognition is long overdue rather than premature, but the elapsed time also means some key people have died.
uncertainties: Credit is divided between X-ray localisation and optical/radio identification, and the supplied names do not cover the entire decisive set.
The deceased cannot be recognised, which may exclude some decisive contributors, and I have not independently verified who among the listed individuals is living.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations, imprinted by sound waves in the early plasma, provide a standard ruler whose detection in galaxy clustering (SDSS and 2dFGRS) in 2005 gave a robust geometric measurement of the expansion history. They underpin the dark-energy programme and, more recently, DESI results. The physics is clean and the scientific use is wide.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein and collaborators led the SDSS luminous-red-galaxy detection, and Cole and the 2dFGRS team made a contemporaneous detection. Sunyaev is credited here for early theoretical work on the acoustic signature, which he developed with Zeldovich, and Peebles and Yu predicted the feature in 1970; these distinctions complicate any prize configuration. I choose the two observational names, accepting that the theory attribution is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The detection has been confirmed repeatedly by BOSS, eBOSS, WiggleZ and DESI, and the technique is a pillar of precision cosmology. Recognition would be timely, although the 2011 prize already recognised the accelerating expansion that BAO complements.
uncertainties: Attribution between the theoretical prediction (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) and the observational detection is contested and cannot be resolved with the supplied names alone.
Whether recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy affect how the committee views the technique is an open question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new class of quantum matter, with theoretical prediction (Kane and Mele; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang) and experimental demonstration in HgTe quantum wells. It has had very large influence across condensed matter, including topological band theory and spintronics concepts. The importance and originality are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane's theoretical work and Molenkamp's experimental observation in HgTe form the decisive pair in this candidate. Other major contributors (Mele, Zhang, Bernevig, Hasan, Xue) are either not on this candidate's list or are placed under a different ballot entry, and the overlap between the two topological-insulator and quantum anomalous Hall candidates complicates allocation.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is extensive, including ARPES observations of three-dimensional topological insulators and the quantum anomalous Hall effect, but the field is mature enough that recognition arguably could have come earlier. The relative closeness to other recent topological prizes (2016) may reduce the room.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the other topological-insulator candidate and with the 2016 Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz prize is unresolved.
Practical applications of the effect remain limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2023 evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays by NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and CPTA opened a new gravitational-wave frequency band, and is likely to be interpreted as supermassive black-hole binaries or possibly new physics. Instrumental precision, long-baseline timing and decades of patient observation are impressive, and I have sympathy for such long-duration instrument work.
assessment.attribution: The array approach involved three regional collaborations whose leaders (McLaughlin for NANOGrav, Kramer for EPTA, Manchester for PPTA) are plausible representatives, but credit also belongs to the founders of pulsar timing (Hellings and Downs, Detweiler, Foster and Backer) and to the many observers. The three supplied names are a defensible choice, but not clearly decisive.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is at roughly three to four sigma, mainly from the Hellings-Downs correlation, without detection of an individual source or a clear spectral identification. This is premature in comparison to a conclusive five-sigma detection, so I place it lower than mature candidates.
uncertainties: The significance is below the usual discovery standard and the origin of the signal is uncertain.
The allocation among the four collaborations and the earlier theory founders is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics implemented strong light-matter coupling with superconducting qubits in microwave resonators, providing the architecture for readout and control in superconducting quantum processors. It is a major concept with practical and fundamental impact, though the 2025 physics prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, which may reduce appetite for another prize in this area soon.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theoretical proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and first experiment (Wallraff et al., Schoelkopf group) are widely cited. Schoelkopf and Wallraff led the experiments; Blais and Girvin led the theory. Since a three-person limit applies, I would select the experimentalists, but the theory partners have a strong claim.
assessment.maturity: The architecture is validated by many groups and is the basis of commercial devices, so it is mature. Timing relative to the 2025 prize is a consideration.
uncertainties: Whether this is sufficiently distinct from the 2025 recognition of superconducting-circuit quantum behaviour.
Allocation between theorists and experimentalists is difficult with a four-person candidate.
